headline: Analyst Ben Reitzes of Melius Research upgraded Microsoft's shares to "buy" on Monday and raised his price target to $665.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a single analyst's rating change, reported by IBD and others, with limited effect beyond one stock.
importance_line: Microsoft shareholders saw the stock rise 1.5% on the day, but an analyst upgrade is one firm's opinion, not a change in Microsoft's results.
summary: Investor's Business Daily reports that Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft to "buy" from "hold" on Monday, raising his price target to $665 from $465, as the software giant is seen as a leader in trustworthiness in AI, and that Microsoft shares rose 1.5% to close at $525.18. Stocktwits, citing the news service TheFly, adds that Melius says worry about AI risks could make Microsoft and cybersecurity companies more important, as businesses pay for secure tools that route AI models to the right task and protect AI agents.
notes: IBD page returns only its first paragraph (paywall); further detail from Stocktwits (citing TheFly) on TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/stocktwits:07812046b094b:0-msft-gets-a-bullish-call-from-melius-analyst-says-ai-fears-could-benefit-leaders-like-microsoft/). Benzinga blocked (Cloudflare 403). Analyst opinion.
